title: Finance and Corporate Services Committee - April 20, 2026

items.title: Commencement
notes: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee held a meeting this date commencing at 2:09 p.m.

items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest and the General Nature Thereof
Consent Items
notes: Pursuant to Chapter 25 (Procedure) of the Municipal Code, a motion was brought forward by Councillor D. Chapman to discuss Consent items 3.1 and 3.2 listed on the agenda, which was voted on and was Carried.

items.title: Surplus Land Declaration and Land Disposition - 5 Charles Street East, DSD-2026-072
notes:
The Committee considered Development Services Department report, DSD-2026-072 recommending that 5 Charles Street East be declared surplus land and severed, with said severed parcel offered for sale to Benton Communities LP; and, that the Mayor and Clerk be authorized to execute an agreement with Benton Communities LP to provide Benton Communities LP with a 3-year option to acquire a remnant surface parking lot at 5 Charles Street East; and, that the Mayor and Clerk be authorized to execute a lease agreement with Benton Communities LP for a temporary lease agreement for the remnant parking lot located at 5 Charles Street East; and, that the Mayor and Clerk be authorized to execute an agreement with St. Mathews Evangelical Lutheran Church for the City of Kitchener to receive a 10-year transferable option to acquire the parcel of land located at 14 Church St, Kitchener; and further, that the Mayor and Clerk be authorized to execute all documentation required to complete said transactions, satisfactory to the City Solicitor.

B. Bennett and C. Bluhm were in attendance and responded to questions from the Committee. 

B. Bennett was recognized for over 13 years of service at the City of Kitchener.

items.title: Corporate Policy Review - New Policies, Amendments and Repeal, COR-2026-154
notes:
The Committee considered Corporate Services Department report, COR-2026-154, dated December 11, 2025 recommending that the corporate policies listed in Appendix A to Corporate Services report COR-2026-154 be amended or repealed; and, that the Data Policy, attached as Appendix B to Corporate Services report COR-2026-154 be approved; and further, that the Body Worn Camera Policy attached as Appendix C to Corporate Services report COR-2026-154 be approved; and further that the Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) Policy attached as Appendix D to Corporate Services report COR-2026-154 be approved.

H. Fylactou, S. Vrentzos and C. Ernst were in attendance and responded to questions from the Committee.

items.title: Council Compensation Review Findings, CAO-2026-172
notes:
The Committee considered Chief Administrative Office report, CAO-2026-172, dated April 8, 2026 recommending that the council compensation recommendations prepared by Marianne Love Consulting Services Ltd., as appended to staff report CAO-2026-172, be approved effective for the 2026-2030 term of council; and that staff be directed to amend GOV-COU-020 (Council Compensation) in accordance with report CAO-2026-172.

J. Watkins provided opening remarks and M. Love, the City's Consultant provided a presentation on her recommendations outlined in the staff report. 

Councillor P. Singh left the meeting at this time.

Councillor B. Ioannidis brought forward a motion to approve the Staff recommendation outlined in report CAO-2026-172 including an amendment that the differential between the 50th and 60th percentile identified in report CAO-2026-172 be funded through an allocation from municipal enterprises, primarily Kitchener Utilities, in recognition of Kitchener Council’s unique governing responsibility for the municipally-owned gas utility. 

Councillor P. Singh re-entered the meeting at this time. 

Mayor B. Vrbanovic brought forward an amendment that the next Council Compensation review be completed prior to the 2030 Election Period and should include all considerations raised through the compensation report presented by Marianne Love Consulting Services Ltd. 

Mayor B. Vrbanovic brought forward a further amendment that the Mayor's compensation be held to an increase of 10.3% which is comparable to the proposed increase for the City Councillors. 

P. Singh left the meeting at this time and re-entered. 

It was requested that all motions be voted on separately and on a recorded vote. 

Councillor B. Ioannidis' amendment related to the 50th and 60th percentile was then voted on and was Carried on a recorded vote with Mayor B. Vrbanovic and Councillors S. Davey, J. Deneault, B. Ioannidis, D. Schnider, P. Singh and S. Stretch voting in favour; and, Councillors C. Michaud and D. Chapman voting in opposition.

Mayor B. Vrbanovic's amendment related to the Council Compensation review prior to 2030 was then voted on and was Carried unanimously on a recorded vote.

Mayor B. Vrbanovic's amendment related to the Mayor's compensation being held to 10.3% was then voted and was Carried, on a recorded vote with Mayor B. Vrbanovic, Councillors D. Chapman, C. Michaud, D. Schnider and P. Singh voting in favour; and, Councillors S. Davey, J. Deneault, B. Ioannidis and S. Stretch voting in opposition.

The following motion as amended was then voted on.

It was noted the recommendation arising from this matter would be considered for ratification at the Special Council meeting later this date.

items.title: Waterloo Region Police Services (WRPS) - Closed Circuit Television and Automatic License Plate Readers Project, DSD-2026-167
notes:
The Committee considered Development Services Department report, DSD-2026-167, dated April 7, 2026 recommending that the City of Kitchener support Waterloo Regional Police Service’s proposed Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) and Automatic License Plant Reader Program (ALPR); and, that the Chief Administrative Officer be authorized to execute an agreement between the City of Kitchener and Waterloo Regional Police Services (WRPS) for the use municipal infrastructure to support the proposed CCTV and ALPR program; and further, that staff report back after a period of one year from the start of the program to discuss the initial results of the CCTV/ALPR program in Kitchener to inform the consideration of an extension of the agreement.

The Committee considered written submissions from the Downtown Kitchener Business Improvement Area and the Fairview Park Mall. 

B. Cronkite and C. Ernst were in attendance to respond to questions from the Committee.

J. Davis, Deputy Chief, Investigations and Operation Support, Waterloo Region Police Services provided a presentation on this matter. J. Brown, Inspector, Innovation and Modernization and D. Mullock, Manager, Government Relations were also in attendance to respond to questions from the Committee. 

In response to questions from the Committee regarding the use of surveillance footage collected from CCTVs, J. Davis advised the Committee that the WRPS will report quarterly to the WRPS Police Services Board on the use of CCTV and ALPR data. It was further noted that videos collected through the proposed CCTV program will be monitored passively by the WRPS Real-Time Operations Centre and would not be accessible to members of WRPS unless they are authorized access to specific videos for matters of criminal interest. 

Councillor C. Michaud left the meeting at this time and re-entered.

Councillor B. Ioannidis left the meeting at this time and re-entered.

The Committee stated privacy concerns with the use of surveillance footage and community acceptance of the CCTV and the ALPR program; and further noted that, as a report will be made to Kitchener's City Council on the outcome of the program one year following implementation, City Council will have an opportunity to determine whether to continue the CCTV/ALPR program. 

Councillor J. Deneault brought forward a motion to approve the recommendation outlined in report DSD-2026-167.

Councillor D. Chapman brought forward a motion to defer consideration of the Staff recommendation outlined in report DSD-2026-167 to the May 4, 2026 Council meeting. 

Councillor M. Johnston re-entered the meeting at this time.

Mayor B. Vrbanovic left the meeting at this time.

It was requested that all motions be voted on, on a recorded vote. 

Councillor D. Chapman's motion to defer was then voted on and LOST on a recorded vote with Councillors D. Chapman, S. Davey and S. Stretch voting in favour; and, Councillors D. Schnider, J. Deneault, C. Michaud, P. Singh, B. Ioannidis and M. Johnston voting in opposition.

The following motion was then voted on.

motions.item_title: Surplus Land Declaration and Land Disposition - 5 Charles Street East, DSD-2026-072
motions.text: it was resolved: "That 5 Charles Street East be declared surplus to the City of Kitchener’s needs; and, That 5 Charles Street East be severed to create a 0.194 acre parcel of land (8,475 square feet) as depicted in Development Services Department report DSD-2026-072, to be further described on a Reference Plan to be prepared in the future, with said severed parcel offered for sale to Benton Communities LP; and, That the Mayor and Clerk be authorized to execute an Agreement of Purchase and Sale with Benton Communities LP for the sale of the City’s severed parcel of land located at 5 Charles Street East, having an area of approximately 0.194 acres (8,475 square feet), legally known as PT LT 3-4, 10-15 PL 394 KITCHENER AS IN 460184 & A102408 S OF 223739; KITCHENER (BEING ALL OF PIN 22501-0008) at a total purchase price of $2,032,746.00; with said agreement to be to the satisfaction of the City Solicitor; and, That the Mayor and Clerk be authorized to execute an agreement with St Mathews Evangelical Lutheran Church for the City of Kitchener to receive a 10-year transferable option to acquire the parcel of land located at 14 Church Street, Kitchener; and, That the Mayor and Clerk be authorized to execute an agreement with Benton Communities LP to provide Benton Communities LP with a 3-year option to acquire the 0.23 acre (10,072 square feet) remnant surface parking lot at 5 Charles Street East in accordance with Development Services Department report DSD-2026-072, for the sole purpose of accommodating a future redevelopment of said lands; and, That the Mayor and Clerk be authorized to execute a lease agreement with Benton Communities LP for a temporary lease agreement for the 0.23 acre (10,072 sq ft) remanent parking lot located at 5 Charles Street East, for the sole purpose of using said lands for construction staging; and further, That the Mayor and Clerk be authorized to execute all other documentation required to complete the transaction, with said documentation to be satisfactory to the City Solicitor."
